claims.text: The starting feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder.
Optimizing laser power and scan speed during additive manufacturing reduces residual thermal stress in AlCrFeNiSi.
Optimizing laser power and scan speed during additive manufacturing reduces defect formation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser-power and scan-speed optimization controls thermal gradients during additive manufacturing.
Laser-power and scan-speed optimization controls solidification rates during additive manufacturing.
Reduced residual thermal stress and defect formation improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Optimized additive manufacturing will increase the yield strength of AlCrFeNiSi by 15% relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
The hypothesis is bounded to laser powers of 200–400 W, scan speeds of 500–1000 mm/s, and temperatures of 20–100 °C.
The optimal laser power and scan speed may vary with the additive-manufacturing system and powder feedstock.
Failure of optimized samples to achieve at least 10% higher yield strength than non-optimized additively manufactured samples is proposed as the falsification criterion.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 15% yield-strength increase relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, but the falsification experiment uses non-optimized additively manufactured material as the comparator and a 10% threshold. Thus, its stated rule does not decisively test the stated prediction.
